records.source: וַיַּאַסְפ֨וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֤ים אֶת־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶם֙ לַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וַיֵּאָ֣סְפ֔וּ שֹׂכֹ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִיהוּדָ֑ה וַֽיַּחֲנ֛וּ בֵּין־שׂוֹכֹ֥ה וּבֵין־עֲזֵקָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥פֶס דַּמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And gathered [the] Philistines their armies for battle, and they were gathered [at] Socoh which [belongs] to Judah, and they encamped between Socoh and between Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.
pieces: The Philistines brought their forces together for war. They assembled at Socoh in Judah and made camp at Ephes-dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.

L.1: And the Philistines gathered their armies for battle, and they were gathered at Socoh, which [belongs] to Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim.

R.1: The Philistines gathered their armies to fight against Israel. They came together at Socoh, a town in Judah, and set up camp at Ephes-dammim, between the towns of Socoh and Azekah.

decisions.choice: Socoh and Azekah: towns of Judah in the low hills west of the mountains
decisions.reason: Both towns are listed among the towns of Judah's lowland (Joshua 15:33-35). They stood above the Valley of Elah (verse 2), one of the routes from the Philistine plain up into the hill country of Judah, so a Philistine army here was pushing into Israel's land.

decisions.choice: Ephes-dammim: a place name
decisions.reason: The two words form one name. The same place seems to be called Pas-dammim in 1 Chronicles 11:13, where David's warriors again fight the Philistines. Its exact site is not known.

decisions.choice: to fight against Israel; the towns of
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the Philistines meant to fight and makes clear that Socoh and Azekah are towns.

records.heading: The Philistine champion's challenge

records.source: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְאִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ נֶאֶסְפ֔וּ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּעֵ֣מֶק הָאֵלָ֑ה וַיַּעַרְכ֥וּ מִלְחָמָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And Saul and [the] men of Israel were gathered and encamped in [the] valley of the Elah, and drew up battle to meet [the] Philistines.
pieces: Saul and the men of Israel also came together. They pitched camp in the Valley of Elah and formed their battle line facing the Philistines.

L.2: And Saul and the men of Israel were gathered, and they camped in the Valley of Elah and drew up [the] battle line to meet the Philistines.

R.2: Saul and the army of Israel also gathered. They camped in the Valley of Elah and got into position for battle, facing the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the Valley of Elah: "the valley of the terebinth"
decisions.reason: The name means "valley of the terebinth", a large spreading tree. It is a broad valley running west from the hills of Judah toward the Philistine plain, past Socoh and Azekah (verse 1).

decisions.choice: the men of Israel: Israel's fighting men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the man of Israel", a collective for the whole body of Israel's soldiers. The same phrase returns in verses 19, 24, 25 and 52.

decisions.choice: the army of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable names the group the collective phrase refers to.

records.source: וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֞ים עֹמְדִ֤ים אֶל־הָהָר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל עֹמְדִ֥ים אֶל־הָהָ֖ר מִזֶּ֑ה וְהַגַּ֖יְא בֵּינֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And [the] Philistines [were] standing on the mountain on this [side], and Israel [were] standing on the mountain on this [side], and the valley [was] between them.
pieces: The Philistines held the hill on one side and Israel held the hill on the other, with the valley between them.

L.3: And the Philistines were standing on the hill on one side, and Israel was standing on the hill on the other side, and the valley [was] between them.

R.3: The Philistines stood on a hill on one side of the valley, and the Israelites stood on a hill on the other side. The valley lay between them.

decisions.choice: the mountain: the high ground on each side of the valley
decisions.reason: The word often means a mountain, but here it is the slope or ridge rising on each side of the Valley of Elah. Neither army could attack without first going down into the open valley, which explains the long standoff (verse 16).

decisions.choice: on one side ... on the other side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "on this [side]" twice; English says "one ... the other".

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֤א אִֽישׁ־הַבֵּנַ֨יִם֙ מִמַּחֲנ֣וֹת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים גָּלְיָ֥ת שְׁמ֖וֹ מִגַּ֑ת גָּבְה֕וֹ שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת וָזָֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And came out the man of the in-between from [the] camps of [the] Philistines, Goliath [was] his name, from Gath; his height [was] six cubits and a span.
pieces: Then a champion came out from the Philistine camp. His name was Goliath, and he was from Gath. He was {{units:about 9 feet 9 inches|six cubits and a span}} tall.

L.4: And the man of the [space] between came out from the camps of the Philistines; Goliath [was] his name, from Gath. His height [was] six cubits and a span.

R.4: A champion fighter named Goliath came out from the Philistine camp. He was from the city of Gath, and he was {{units:about 9 feet 9 inches|six cubits and a span}} tall.

decisions.choice: the man of the space between: a champion
decisions.reason: The phrase describes a warrior who stepped out into the open ground between the two battle lines to fight a single opponent, so that one fight could settle the battle (verses 8-9). It is found only in this chapter (also verse 23).

decisions.choice: six cubits and a span
decisions.reason: The received Hebrew text reads "six cubits and a span", about 9 feet 9 inches. The ancient Greek translation, a Hebrew manuscript of Samuel found at Qumran, and the historian Josephus read "four cubits and a span", about 6 feet 9 inches, still a giant of a man in that age. Either reading may be original. This note is given from general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check it against a critical edition before the sentence is marked reviewed.

decisions.choice: a cubit is about 18 inches; a span about 9 inches
decisions.reason: The cubit was the length from the elbow to the fingertip, and the span the width of the spread hand from thumb to little finger, about half a cubit (Exodus 28:16).

decisions.choice: Gath: one of the five Philistine cities
decisions.reason: Gath was one of the five chief cities of the Philistines (6:17). Joshua 11:22 says that some of the Anakim, a people remembered for their great size, were left in Gath.

decisions.choice: modern measure with the cubits as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the height in feet and inches, with the original cubits and span as a setting. Literal keeps the original units.

decisions.choice: a champion; a champion fighter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the phrase that Literal keeps word for word.

records.source: וְכ֤וֹבַע נְחֹ֨שֶׁת֙ עַל־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְשִׁרְי֥וֹן קַשְׂקַשִּׂ֖ים ה֣וּא לָב֑וּשׁ וּמִשְׁקַל֙ הַשִּׁרְי֔וֹן חֲמֵשֶׁת־אֲלָפִ֥ים שְׁקָלִ֖ים נְחֹֽשֶֽׁת׃
records.gloss: And a helmet of bronze [was] on his head, and armor of scales he [was] clothed [in], and the weight of the armor [was] five thousand shekels of bronze.
pieces: He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a coat of scale armor made of bronze that weighed {{units:about 125 pounds|5,000 shekels}}.

L.5: And a helmet of bronze [was] on his head, and he was clothed [in] armor of scales, and the weight of the armor [was] 5,000 shekels of bronze.

R.5: He wore a bronze helmet. His body armor was made of small overlapping pieces of bronze, and it weighed {{units:about 125 pounds|5,000 shekels}}.

decisions.choice: armor of scales: a coat of small overlapping metal plates
decisions.reason: The second word is the one used for the scales of a fish (Leviticus 11:9). The coat was made of many small plates sewn on in rows, like scales. Saul has such a coat too (verse 38).

decisions.choice: 5,000 shekels: about 125 pounds
decisions.reason: A shekel weighed about 2/5 ounce, so the coat weighed about 125 pounds. The writer lists Goliath's weapons and their weights to show how strong and well armed he was, all of which counts for nothing in verses 45-50.

decisions.choice: a coat ... made of bronze that weighed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the coat was made of before its weight, since the weight is given as a setting span.

decisions.choice: modern weight with the shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the weight in pounds; Literal keeps the shekels.

records.source: וּמִצְחַ֥ת נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־רַגְלָ֑יו וְכִיד֥וֹן נְחֹ֖שֶׁת בֵּ֥ין כְּתֵפָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And greaves of bronze [were] on his feet, and a javelin of bronze [was] between his shoulders.
pieces: He had bronze guards on his legs, and a bronze javelin was slung across his back.

L.6: And greaves of bronze [were] on his feet, and a javelin of bronze [was] between his shoulders.

R.6: Bronze armor protected his legs, and he carried a bronze javelin on his back.

decisions.choice: greaves: armor for the lower legs
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It names plates that covered the shins; "on his feet" means on his legs, as the word for feet can include the legs.

decisions.choice: javelin: a short throwing spear
decisions.reason: The same weapon is held out by Joshua in Joshua 8:18 and is named with the sword and spear in verse 45. Some take it to be a curved sword instead. Either way it was a second weapon besides the great spear of verse 7.

decisions.choice: between his shoulders: on his back
decisions.reason: The weapon was carried slung across the back.

decisions.choice: bronze guards on his legs; bronze armor protected his legs
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the greaves, since the word is unfamiliar.

records.source: וְעֵ֣ץ חֲנִית֗וֹ כִּמְנוֹר֙ אֹֽרְגִ֔ים וְלַהֶ֣בֶת חֲנִית֔וֹ שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בַּרְזֶ֑ל וְנֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה הֹלֵ֥ךְ לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And [the] shaft of his spear [was] like a beam of weavers, and [the] blade of his spear [was] six hundred shekels of iron; and the bearer of the shield [was] walking before him.
pieces: His spear had a shaft like a weaver's beam, with an iron head that weighed {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}}. A man carrying his shield walked in front of him.

L.7: And the shaft of his spear [was] like a weavers' beam, and the blade of his spear [was] 600 shekels of iron; and the bearer of the shield [was] walking before him.

R.7: The pole of his spear was like the heavy beam of a weaver's loom, and its iron point alone weighed {{units:about 15 pounds|600 shekels}}. A soldier carrying Goliath's large shield walked in front of him.

decisions.choice: the shaft (wood) of his spear
decisions.reason: The letters written in the text spell a word for "arrow", but the tradition of reading marks them to be read as "wood", that is, the shaft of the spear. The text followed here reads "shaft", as the parallel in 2 Samuel 21:19 has it.

decisions.choice: like a weavers' beam: a huge, heavy shaft
alternatives: a spear with a loop and cord for throwing
decisions.reason: A weaver's beam was the wooden bar of a loom. The comparison may be to its thickness, or to the loop of cord tied to the bar, since some spears had a loop and cord that made them spin when thrown. The same picture is used of other giants (2 Samuel 21:19; 1 Chronicles 11:23).

decisions.choice: 600 shekels of iron: about 15 pounds
decisions.reason: The point alone weighed about 15 pounds. Iron was costly in Israel at this time, and the Philistines kept control of metalworking (13:19-22).

decisions.choice: the shield: a large body shield
decisions.reason: This is the big shield that covered the whole body, carried by an attendant who walked in front of the warrior (also verse 41). It is a different word from the small round shield.

decisions.choice: modern weight with the shekels as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

decisions.choice: its iron point alone; Goliath's large shield
decisions.reason: Readable adds "alone" to show that this was only the point, and names whose shield was carried.

records.source: וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֗ד וַיִּקְרָא֙ אֶל־מַעַרְכֹ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לָ֥מָּה תֵצְא֖וּ לַעֲרֹ֣ךְ מִלְחָמָ֑ה הֲל֧וֹא אָנֹכִ֣י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֗י וְאַתֶּם֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים לְשָׁא֔וּל בְּרוּ־לָכֶ֥ם אִ֖ישׁ וְיֵרֵ֥ד אֵלָֽי׃
records.gloss: And he stood and called out to [the] ranks of Israel and said to them, Why do you come out to draw up battle? [Am] not I the Philistine, and you servants of Saul? Choose for yourselves a man, and let him come down to me.
pieces: He stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, "Why have you come out and lined up for battle? I am the Philistine, and you are Saul's servants, are you not? Pick a man for yourselves and let him come down to me.

L.8: And he stood and called out to the ranks of Israel and said to them, "Why do you come out to draw up [for] battle? [Am] I not the Philistine, and you servants of Saul? Choose a man for yourselves, and let him come down to me.

R.8: Goliath stood and shouted to Israel's soldiers, "Why are you lining up for battle? I am the Philistine champion, and you are only Saul's servants. Choose one of your men and send him down to me.

decisions.choice: Am I not the Philistine, and you servants of Saul?: a taunt
decisions.reason: Goliath sets himself, the Philistine champion, against men who are only the servants of a king. He scorns them as men who fight for another, not for themselves.

decisions.choice: choose a man: a challenge to single combat
decisions.reason: Instead of a battle between whole armies, each side would send one fighter, and the result would decide the war (verse 9). The same kind of contest is told in 2 Samuel 2:14-16.

decisions.choice: the ranks of Israel: Israel's army drawn up for battle
decisions.reason: The word means battle lines, troops set in order. It recurs through the chapter (verses 10, 26, 36, 45) and is joined with "the living God" and "the God of the ranks of Israel".

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: Here the word means the king's men, his subjects and soldiers, so "servants" is kept at every level, as for the king's servants elsewhere in Samuel.

decisions.choice: Goliath; champion; only
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, says what he means by "the Philistine", and adds "only" to bring out the scorn.

records.source: אִם־יוּכַ֞ל לְהִלָּחֵ֤ם אִתִּי֙ וְהִכָּ֔נִי וְהָיִ֥ינוּ לָכֶ֖ם לַעֲבָדִ֑ים וְאִם־אֲנִ֤י אֽוּכַל־לוֹ֙ וְהִכִּיתִ֔יו וִהְיִ֤יתֶם לָ֨נוּ֙ לַעֲבָדִ֔ים וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֖ם אֹתָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: If he is able to fight with me and strikes me down, then we will become to you slaves; but if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you will become to us slaves and serve us.
pieces: If he can fight me and kill me, we will be your slaves. But if I defeat him and kill him, you will be our slaves and serve us."

L.9: If he is able to fight with me and strikes me down, then we will become your slaves; but if I prevail over him and strike him down, then you will become our slaves and serve us."

R.9: If he wins the fight and kills me, we Philistines will become your slaves. But if I win and kill him, you Israelites will become our slaves and work for us."

decisions.choice: we will become your slaves: the whole nation bound by one fight
decisions.reason: The loser's people would be subject to the winner's people. When Goliath falls, the Philistines do not keep these terms; they run (verses 51-52).

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" is kept at every level because Goliath speaks of one people being made subject to another, where slavery itself is the point (as in Exodus 20:2).

decisions.choice: we Philistines; you Israelites
decisions.reason: Readable names the two peoples meant by "we" and "you".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אֲנִ֗י חֵרַ֛פְתִּי אֶת־מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה תְּנוּ־לִ֣י אִ֔ישׁ וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה יָֽחַד׃
records.gloss: And said the Philistine, I defy the ranks of Israel this day; give to me a man, and let us fight together.
pieces: And the Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel today! Give me a man, and we will fight each other."

L.10: And the Philistine said, "I defy the ranks of Israel this day. Give me a man, and let us fight together."

R.10: The Philistine said, "Today I am mocking Israel's army. Send me a man to fight me one on one!"

decisions.choice: defy: taunt, insult, put to shame
decisions.reason: The verb means to scorn and shame someone with words. It is a key word in this chapter (verses 25, 26, 36, 45): David hears the taunt as an insult to the living God, whose army this is.

decisions.choice: mocking; one on one
decisions.reason: Readable uses a common word for the taunt and spells out what "fight together" means here.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע שָׁאוּל֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחַ֥תּוּ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃פ
records.gloss: And heard Saul and all Israel these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and were afraid greatly.
pieces: When Saul and all Israel heard what the Philistine said, they were shaken and terrified.

L.11: And Saul and all Israel heard these words of the Philistine, and they were dismayed and greatly afraid.

R.11: When Saul and all the Israelites heard what the Philistine said, they lost heart and were very afraid.

decisions.choice: dismayed and afraid: the opposite of what God had told Israel
decisions.reason: The same two verbs are used when God and Moses tell Israel and Joshua not to be afraid or dismayed (Deuteronomy 1:21; 31:8; Joshua 1:9; 8:1). Israel's army reacts in the very way it was told not to.

decisions.choice: Saul is afraid
decisions.reason: Saul was taller than anyone in Israel (9:2; 10:23), and the people wanted a king to go out before them and fight their battles (8:20). Now the tall king does not go out; a shepherd boy will.

decisions.choice: shaken; lost heart
decisions.reason: The verb means to be shattered or broken in spirit. Balanced and Readable choose words that show fear taking away the will to fight.

records.source: וְדָוִד֩ בֶּן־אִ֨ישׁ אֶפְרָתִ֜י הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּ֥ית לֶ֨חֶם֙ יְהוּדָ֔ה וּשְׁמ֣וֹ יִשַׁ֔י וְל֖וֹ שְׁמֹנָ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וְהָאִישׁ֙ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁא֔וּל זָקֵ֖ן בָּ֥א בַאֲנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And David [was the] son of an Ephrathite man, this [one], from Bethlehem of Judah, and his name [was] Jesse, and to him [were] eight sons; and the man in [the] days of Saul [was] old, gone among men.
pieces: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse. Jesse had eight sons, and in Saul's time he was already old, advanced in years.

L.12: And David [was the] son of this Ephrathite man from Bethlehem of Judah, whose name [was] Jesse, and he had eight sons; and in the days of Saul the man was old, advanced among men.

R.12: David was the son of Jesse, a man of the Ephrathah clan who lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons. By the time Saul was king, Jesse was an old man.

decisions.choice: the received Hebrew text, with verses 12-31
decisions.reason: The oldest manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation have a much shorter form of this chapter. They lack verses 12-31, 41, 50 and 55-58, and part of verse 48, as well as parts of chapter 18. In that shorter story David is already Saul's armor-bearer (16:21), and the account runs straight from Goliath's challenge (verse 11) to David's offer to fight (verse 32). The longer Hebrew text tells a second line of the story: David the shepherd boy who comes to the camp with food, and whom Saul does not know (verses 55-58). It may be that the Greek translators, or the Hebrew text they used, left out what seemed to repeat or not fit chapter 16, or that the Hebrew text joined two accounts of how David came to Saul. The received Hebrew text is followed here. This note is given from general knowledge of the manuscripts; reviewers must check it against a critical edition.

decisions.choice: this Ephrathite: the Jesse already named
decisions.reason: "This" points back to Jesse, who was introduced in 16:1-13. The verse reintroduces David's family, as if starting a new account.

decisions.choice: Ephrathite: of Ephrathah, the clan and district of Bethlehem
decisions.reason: Ephrathah is an old name for Bethlehem and its clan (Genesis 35:19; Ruth 1:2; 4:11; Micah 5:1).

decisions.choice: gone among men: advanced in years
alternatives: came among the men (of the army)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew phrase is unusual; it seems to mean that Jesse had come to be counted among the old men. The ancient Greek and other early translations read "advanced in years". The point is that Jesse was too old to go to war himself, so his sons went (verse 13).

decisions.choice: David was the son of Jesse, a man of the Ephrathah clan
decisions.reason: Readable gives Jesse's name first and explains "Ephrathite".

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת בְּנֵֽי־יִשַׁי֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֥וּ אַחֲרֵי־שָׁא֖וּל לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֣ם׀שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת בָּנָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָלְכוּ֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה אֱלִיאָ֣ב הַבְּכ֗וֹר וּמִשְׁנֵ֨הוּ֙ אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖י שַׁמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And went the three sons of Jesse, the older [ones], [they] went after Saul to the battle; and [the] name of his three sons who went into the battle [were] Eliab the firstborn, and his second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.
pieces: Jesse's three oldest sons had followed Saul to the war. The names of the three who went to war were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third.

L.13: And the three oldest sons of Jesse had gone; they had gone after Saul to the battle. And the names of his three sons who went into the battle [were] Eliab the firstborn, and his second Abinadab, and the third Shammah.

R.13: His three oldest sons had gone with Saul to fight in the war. The oldest was Eliab, the next was Abinadab, and the third was Shammah.

decisions.choice: Eliab, Abinadab and Shammah: the sons passed over in 16:6-9
decisions.reason: These are the three sons whom Samuel saw first and whom Yahweh did not choose (16:6-10). They are now soldiers in Saul's army, while the chosen youngest tends the sheep.

decisions.choice: went after Saul: followed him to war
decisions.reason: To go after a leader is to follow him as one of his fighting men.

records.source: וְדָוִ֖ד ה֣וּא הַקָּטָ֑ן וּשְׁלֹשָׁה֙ הַגְּדֹלִ֔ים הָלְכ֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃ס
records.gloss: And David he [was] the youngest, and [the] three older [ones] went after Saul.
pieces: David was the youngest, and the three oldest had followed Saul.

L.14: And David, he [was] the youngest; and the three oldest had gone after Saul.

R.14: David was the youngest son. His three oldest brothers had gone with Saul.

decisions.choice: the youngest: also "the smallest"
decisions.reason: The word means both youngest and smallest. It is the word Jesse used of David in 16:11, and it sets David against the giant of verse 4.

records.source: וְדָוִ֛ד הֹלֵ֥ךְ וָשָׁ֖ב מֵעַ֣ל שָׁא֑וּל לִרְע֛וֹת אֶת־צֹ֥אן אָבִ֖יו בֵּֽית־לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: And David [was] going and returning from Saul to shepherd the flock of his father [at] Bethlehem.
pieces: David went back and forth from Saul's service to tend his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

L.15: And David was going and returning from Saul to shepherd his father's flock [at] Bethlehem.

R.15: David went back and forth between serving Saul and taking care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.

decisions.choice: going and returning from Saul: back and forth between Saul and home
alternatives: had gone back home from Saul
decisions.reason: The verse links this account with 16:21-23, where David became one of Saul's attendants. He served Saul at times and went home to the sheep at others. It could also mean that David had gone back from Saul's service to the flock for good.

decisions.choice: from Saul's service; between serving Saul and
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that it was Saul's service David left and returned to, as 16:21-22 shows.

records.source: וַיִּגַּ֥שׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַשְׁכֵּ֣ם וְהַעֲרֵ֑ב וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֖ב אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃פ
records.gloss: And drew near the Philistine, rising early and doing evening, and took his stand forty days.
pieces: Meanwhile the Philistine came forward every morning and evening and took his stand, for forty days.

L.16: And the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and he took his stand [for] forty days.

R.16: For forty days the Philistine came out every morning and every evening and stood there, daring Israel to fight.

decisions.choice: rising early and doing evening: morning and evening
decisions.reason: The two verbs mean to do something early in the morning and in the evening: Goliath made his challenge twice each day.

decisions.choice: forty days: a long, full period
decisions.reason: Forty days is a round time often used for a full period of testing (Numbers 13:25; 14:34; Deuteronomy 9:9). For forty days no one in Israel answered the challenge.

decisions.choice: daring Israel to fight
decisions.reason: Readable says why Goliath took his stand, from verses 8-10.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִשַׁ֜י לְדָוִ֣ד בְּנ֗וֹ קַח־נָ֤א לְאַחֶ֨יךָ֙ אֵיפַ֤ת הַקָּלִיא֙ הַזֶּ֔ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֥ה לֶ֖חֶם הַזֶּ֑ה וְהָרֵ֥ץ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לְאַחֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And said Jesse to David his son, Take, please, to your brothers this ephah of the roasted grain and these ten loaves, and bring [them] quickly [to] the camp to your brothers.
pieces: Jesse said to his son David, "Please take {{units:about 20 quarts|this ephah}} of roasted grain and these ten loaves for your brothers, and hurry to the camp with them for your brothers.

L.17: And Jesse said to David his son, "Please take for your brothers this ephah of roasted grain and these ten loaves, and run [them] to the camp to your brothers.

R.17: One day Jesse said to his son David, "Take {{units:about 20 quarts|this ephah}} of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers. Hurry to the army camp and give them to your brothers.

decisions.choice: roasted grain: a staple food for the field
decisions.reason: Heads of grain roasted over a fire were a simple food that kept well (Ruth 2:14; 25:18). Soldiers of the time were often supplied by their own families.

decisions.choice: an ephah: about 20 quarts
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure of about 20 quarts, a large load for one young man.

decisions.choice: modern measure with "this ephah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the measure in quarts, with the original unit as a setting.

decisions.choice: One day
decisions.reason: Readable marks the start of a new scene.

records.heading: David is sent to his brothers

records.source: וְ֠אֵת עֲשֶׂ֜רֶת חֲרִצֵ֤י הֶֽחָלָב֙ הָאֵ֔לֶּה תָּבִ֖יא לְשַׂר־הָאָ֑לֶף וְאֶת־אַחֶ֨יךָ֙ תִּפְקֹ֣ד לְשָׁל֔וֹם וְאֶת־עֲרֻבָּתָ֖ם תִּקָּֽח׃
records.gloss: And these ten portions of the milk you will bring to the commander of the thousand, and your brothers you will visit for welfare, and their pledge you will take.
pieces: Also take these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit. See how your brothers are doing, and bring back some token from them."

L.18: And these ten cuts of milk you will bring to the commander of the thousand; and you will look into your brothers' welfare and take their pledge."

R.18: And take these ten cheeses to their commander. Find out how your brothers are, and bring back something from them to show that they are all right."

decisions.choice: cuts of milk: cheeses
decisions.reason: The phrase names something cut from curdled milk, rounds or slices of soft cheese.

decisions.choice: the commander of the thousand: the officer over their unit
decisions.reason: A "thousand" was a unit of the army under its commander (8:12; 18:13). The unit may not have numbered a full thousand men (see the note at Numbers 1:21). The gift of cheese was likely meant to win the officer's favor for the brothers.

decisions.choice: their pledge: some token from them
decisions.reason: The word means a pledge or token. It may mean a sign that the brothers were well and had received the food, or something they had left as a pledge that could now be redeemed. The exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: ten cheeses; the commander of their unit; their commander
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the food plainly and describe the officer's rank without the unit's size.

records.source: וְשָׁא֤וּל וְהֵ֨מָּה֙ וְכָל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּעֵ֖מֶק הָֽאֵלָ֑ה נִלְחָמִ֖ים עִם־פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And Saul and they and every man of Israel [were] in the valley of the Elah, fighting with [the] Philistines.
pieces: Saul was in the Valley of Elah with the brothers and all the men of Israel, at war with the Philistines.

L.19: And Saul and they and all the men of Israel [were] in the Valley of Elah, fighting with the Philistines.

R.19: Saul, David's brothers and the whole army of Israel were in the Valley of Elah, fighting against the Philistines.

decisions.choice: the narrator's words
decisions.reason: This verse could be the end of Jesse's words, telling David where to find his brothers, or the narrator's note. It is read here as the narrator's, since Jesse has finished his instructions.

decisions.choice: fighting: at war, though no battle had yet been fought
decisions.reason: The word describes the state of war: the armies were drawn up against each other (verses 2-3, 16), but no battle was fought until David's victory.

decisions.choice: the brothers; David's brothers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "they" are.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם דָּוִ֜ד בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּטֹּ֤שׁ אֶת־הַצֹּאן֙ עַל־שֹׁמֵ֔ר וַיִּשָּׂ֣א וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖הוּ יִשָׁ֑י וַיָּבֹא֙ הַמַּעְגָּ֔לָה וְהַחַ֗יִל הַיֹּצֵא֙ אֶל־הַמַּ֣עֲרָכָ֔ה וְהֵרֵ֖עוּ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And rose early David in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and lifted up and went, as had commanded him Jesse; and he came to the encampment, and the army [was] going out to the battle line, and they shouted [the] war cry for battle.
pieces: David got up early in the morning, left the sheep with someone to watch them, loaded up the food, and set out as Jesse had told him. He reached the camp just as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry.

L.20: And David rose early in the morning and left the flock with a keeper, and he loaded up and went as Jesse had commanded him; and he came to the encampment as the army was going out to the battle line, and they were shouting the war cry for battle.

R.20: So David got up early the next morning. He left the sheep with someone to watch them, packed up the food, and went, just as his father Jesse had told him. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were marching out to their battle positions, shouting their battle cry.

decisions.choice: the encampment: the ring of the camp
decisions.reason: The word means a circle or track. It probably names the camp's outer ring, perhaps a circle of carts or a barricade (26:5, 7).

decisions.choice: lifted up: loaded the supplies
decisions.reason: The verb "lift" here means to load and carry the food of verses 17-18.

decisions.choice: shouted the war cry: the loud shout raised before battle
decisions.reason: This is the shout an army gave as it went into battle (Joshua 6:5, 20; and 4:5 in this book).

decisions.choice: his father Jesse
decisions.reason: Readable reminds the reader who Jesse is.

records.source: וַתַּעֲרֹ֤ךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֔ים מַעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את מַעֲרָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And drew up Israel and [the] Philistines battle line to meet battle line.
pieces: Israel and the Philistines were drawn up, battle line facing battle line.

L.21: And Israel and the Philistines drew up battle line to meet battle line.

R.21: The Israelites and the Philistines lined up their armies facing each other.

decisions.choice: battle line to meet battle line: the two armies face to face
decisions.reason: The repeated word pictures two ranks facing each other across the valley (verse 3).

decisions.choice: lined up their armies facing each other
decisions.reason: Readable says the picture plainly.

records.source: וַיִּטֹּשׁ֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־הַכֵּלִ֜ים מֵעָלָ֗יו עַל־יַד֙ שׁוֹמֵ֣ר הַכֵּלִ֔ים וַיָּ֖רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל לְאֶחָ֖יו לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And left David the baggage from upon him in [the] hand of the keeper of the baggage, and ran [to] the battle line and came and asked his brothers for welfare.
pieces: David left his load with the keeper of the supplies, ran to the battle line, and went to ask his brothers how they were.

L.22: And David left the baggage from on him in the hand of the keeper of the baggage, and he ran [to] the battle line and came and asked his brothers about [their] welfare.

R.22: David left the food with the man who was guarding the supplies. Then he ran to the battle line to greet his brothers and ask how they were.

decisions.choice: the baggage: the things he carried
decisions.reason: The word means gear or things in general; here it is the food and supplies of verses 17-18. The army kept a guard over its baggage (25:13; 30:24).

decisions.choice: asked his brothers about their welfare: greeted them
decisions.reason: To ask about someone's welfare (shalom) was the usual greeting, and it was also what Jesse sent David to do (verse 18).

records.source: וְה֣וּא׀מְדַבֵּ֣ר עִמָּ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֣ה אִ֣ישׁ הַבֵּנַ֡יִם עוֹלֶ֞ה גָּלְיָת֩ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י שְׁמ֤וֹ מִגַּת֙ מִמַּעַרְכ֣וֹתפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וַיְדַבֵּ֖ר כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיִּשְׁמַ֖ע דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And he [was] speaking with them, and look, the man of the in-between coming up, Goliath the Philistine [was] his name, from Gath, from the battle lines of [the] Philistines, and he spoke according to these words, and David heard.
pieces: While he was talking with them, the champion, the Philistine from Gath named Goliath, came up out of the Philistine ranks and spoke the same words as before, and David heard them.

L.23: And he was speaking with them, and look, the man of the [space] between was coming up, Goliath the Philistine [was] his name, from Gath, out of the ranks of the Philistines; and he spoke the same words, and David heard.

R.23: While David was talking with them, Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, came out from the Philistine army. He shouted the same challenge as before, and David heard it.

decisions.choice: out of the ranks of the Philistines
decisions.reason: The letters written in the text spell a word meaning "caves", but the tradition of reading marks them to be read "battle lines", the word used throughout the chapter. The text followed here reads "battle lines".

decisions.choice: according to these words: the same challenge as before
decisions.reason: Goliath repeats the words of verses 8-10, and now David hears them.

decisions.choice: look: the story turns to what David sees
decisions.reason: The word draws attention to a sudden event, seen as if through the eyes of the person in the story.

decisions.choice: while ... came up (Balanced); left out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable let the sentence carry the surprise rather than use an old-fashioned word for "look".

records.source: וְכֹל֙ אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בִּרְאוֹתָ֖ם אֶת־הָאִ֑ישׁ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ֙ מִפָּנָ֔יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And every man of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from before him and were afraid greatly.
pieces: Whenever the men of Israel saw the man, they all ran from him in great fear.

L.24: And all the men of Israel, when they saw the man, fled from him and were greatly afraid.

R.24: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they all ran away from him, terrified.

decisions.choice: were greatly afraid: as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The same words were used of Saul and all Israel in verse 11. David's response in verses 26 and 32 stands against the fear of the whole army.

decisions.choice: fled from before him: drew back from where he was
decisions.reason: The phrase means to flee from someone's presence. The soldiers fell back each time he came near.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַרְּאִיתֶם֙ הָאִ֤ישׁ הָֽעֹלֶה֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֛י לְחָרֵ֥ף אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֹלֶ֑ה וְֽ֠הָיָה הָאִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יַכֶּ֜נּוּ יַעְשְׁרֶ֥נּוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ׀עֹ֣שֶׁר גָּד֗וֹל וְאֶת־בִּתּוֹ֙ יִתֶּן־ל֔וֹ וְאֵת֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו יַעֲשֶׂ֥ה חָפְשִׁ֖י בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said [the] man of Israel, Have you seen this man who comes up? For to defy Israel he comes up. And it will be, the man who strikes him down, the king will make him rich [with] great riches, and his daughter he will give to him, and the house of his father he will make free in Israel.
pieces: The men of Israel were saying, "Have you seen this man coming up? He comes up to defy Israel! The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will give him his daughter as well, and he will make his father's family free in Israel."

L.25: And the men of Israel said, "Have you seen this man who is coming up? Surely he comes up to defy Israel. And the man who strikes him down, the king will make him rich with great riches, and he will give him his daughter, and he will make his father's house free in Israel."

R.25: The Israelite soldiers were saying to one another, "Do you see this man? He keeps coming out to insult Israel. The king will make the man who kills him very rich. He will also let that man marry his daughter, and his father's family will not have to pay taxes or work for the king anymore."

decisions.choice: the rewards: wealth, the king's daughter, freedom for the family
decisions.reason: The king promises riches, marriage into the royal family (18:17-27) and that the winner's family will be "free". This probably means free from the taxes and forced labor a king could demand (8:11-17).

decisions.choice: surely he comes up to defy Israel
decisions.reason: The small word at the start of the clause stresses it: this man comes up for no other purpose than to taunt Israel.

decisions.choice: will not have to pay taxes or work for the king anymore
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "free" probably means. The exact privileges are not listed in the text.

decisions.choice: were saying to one another
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the soldiers were talking among themselves, as verse 26 shows.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗ד אֶֽל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֞ים הָעֹמְדִ֣ים עִמּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ מַה־יֵּעָשֶׂ֗ה לָאִישׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַכֶּה֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַלָּ֔ז וְהֵסִ֥יר חֶרְפָּ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֣י מִ֗י הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֤י הֶֽעָרֵל֙ הַזֶּ֔ה כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכ֖וֹת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And said David to the men standing with him, saying, What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and removes reproach from upon Israel? For who [is] this uncircumcised Philistine that he has defied [the] ranks of [the] living God?
pieces: David asked the men standing near him, "What will be done for whoever kills this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? This uncircumcised Philistine, who is he, that he dares to defy the ranks of the living God?"

L.26: And David said to the men who were standing with him, "What will be done for the man who strikes down this Philistine and takes away the disgrace from Israel? For who [is] this uncircumcised Philistine, that he has defied the ranks of the living God?"

R.26: David asked the men standing near him, "What will the king do for the man who kills this Philistine and takes away Israel's shame? This Philistine is outside God's covenant. Who does he think he is, insulting the army of the living God?"

decisions.choice: reproach: disgrace
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "defy" in verse 10. As long as no one answers Goliath's taunt, Israel stands disgraced.

decisions.choice: uncircumcised: outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Circumcision was the sign of God's covenant with Abraham's descendants (Genesis 17:10-14). Israel called the Philistines "the uncircumcised" as people outside that covenant (14:6; 31:4; Judges 14:3).

decisions.choice: the living God
decisions.reason: Israel's God is alive and acts, unlike the gods of the nations (Deuteronomy 5:26; Joshua 3:10). David sees that Goliath's taunt is aimed at God, whose army Israel is.

decisions.choice: is outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Readable explains what "uncircumcised" means here, in the wording used for it throughout the book (14:6; 31:4).

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names who will reward the winner, from verse 25.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ הָעָ֔ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה יֵעָשֶׂ֔ה לָאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַכֶּֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: And said to him the people according to this word, saying, Thus will be done for the man who strikes him down.
pieces: The troops repeated to him what they had said: "This is what will be done for the man who kills him."

L.27: And the people spoke to him according to this word, saying, "So it will be done for the man who strikes him down."

R.27: The soldiers told him the same thing again: "That is what the king will do for the man who kills him."

decisions.choice: according to this word: the same words as verse 25
decisions.reason: The soldiers repeat the promises of verse 25.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Readable names who will do it, as in verse 26.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֱלִיאָב֙ אָחִ֣יו הַגָּד֔וֹל בְּדַבְּר֖וֹ אֶל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים וַיִּֽחַר־אַף֩ אֱלִיאָ֨ב בְּדָוִ֜ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀לָמָּה־זֶּ֣ה יָרַ֗דְתָּ וְעַל־מִ֨י נָטַ֜שְׁתָּ מְעַ֨ט הַצֹּ֤אן הָהֵ֨נָּה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֲנִ֧י יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶת־זְדֹנְךָ֗ וְאֵת֙ רֹ֣עַ לְבָבֶ֔ךָ כִּ֗י לְמַ֛עַן רְא֥וֹת הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה יָרָֽדְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And heard Eliab his oldest brother when he spoke to the men, and burned [the] anger of Eliab against David, and he said, Why [is] this [that] you have come down? And with whom have you left those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for to see the battle you have come down.
pieces: When Eliab, his oldest brother, heard him talking to the men, he grew angry with David and said, "Why have you come down here? Who did you leave those few sheep with out in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness in your heart. You have come down for nothing but to see the fighting!"

L.28: And Eliab his oldest brother heard when he spoke to the men, and Eliab's anger burned against David, and he said, "Why have you come down? And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness? I know your presumption and the evil of your heart, for you have come down to see the battle."

R.28: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the men, and he became angry with David. He said, "Why did you come here? Who is taking care of those few sheep out in the wilderness? I know how proud you are and how bad your motives are. You only came to watch the fighting!"

decisions.choice: presumption: pride that reaches above one's place
decisions.reason: The word means arrogance or insolence, thinking oneself more than one is. Eliab thinks his young brother is meddling in the business of soldiers.

decisions.choice: the evil of your heart
decisions.reason: Eliab claims to know David's heart. But Yahweh, who looks at the heart, had passed over Eliab and chosen David (16:7).

decisions.choice: those few sheep: scorn for David's work
decisions.reason: Eliab makes David's flock sound small and his job unimportant, and blames him for leaving it.

decisions.choice: how bad your motives are
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "the evil of your heart": Eliab says David came for a wrong reason.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד מֶ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי עָ֑תָּה הֲל֖וֹא דָּבָ֥ר הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And said David, What have I done now? [Was] it not [only] a word?
pieces: David said, "What have I done now? Can I not even ask a question?"

L.29: And David said, "What have I done now? [Was] it not [only] a word?"

R.29: David answered, "What have I done wrong now? I was only asking a question."

decisions.choice: was it not only a word?: David was just asking
decisions.reason: The words mean "It was only talk": David says he has only asked a question. The word for "word" can also mean "matter" or "reason", so the clause has also been read "Is there not a reason?", that is, a good cause to speak.

decisions.choice: now: once again
decisions.reason: "Now" suggests that Eliab has found fault with David before.

decisions.choice: I was only asking a question
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

records.source: וַיִּסֹּ֤ב מֵֽאֶצְלוֹ֙ אֶל־מ֣וּל אַחֵ֔ר וַיֹּ֖אמֶר כַּדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיְשִׁבֻ֤הוּ הָעָם֙ דָּבָ֔ר כַּדָּבָ֖ר הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃
records.gloss: And he turned from beside him toward another, and said according to this word; and answered him the people word according to the former word.
pieces: He turned away from him to someone else and asked the same thing, and the troops gave him the same answer as before.

L.30: And he turned away from him toward another and spoke according to this word; and the people answered him a word like the first word.

R.30: Then David turned to someone else and asked the same question. And the people gave him the same answer.

decisions.choice: he turned toward another: David ignores Eliab
decisions.reason: David does not argue with his brother but keeps asking. His persistence is how his words reach Saul (verse 31).

records.source: וַיְּשָּֽׁמְעוּ֙הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּגִּ֥דוּ לִפְנֵֽי־שָׁא֖וּל וַיִּקָּחֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And were heard the words which David spoke, and they told [them] before Saul, and he took him.
pieces: What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him.

L.31: And the words that David spoke were heard, and they told [them] before Saul, and he sent for him.

R.31: Some men heard what David was saying and told Saul about it. So Saul sent for David.

decisions.choice: he took him: Saul had him brought
decisions.reason: The verb "take" here means that Saul summoned David and had him brought to him.

decisions.choice: Some men
decisions.reason: Readable supplies a subject for the passive "were heard".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל אַל־יִפֹּ֥ל לֵב־אָדָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו עַבְדְּךָ֣ יֵלֵ֔ךְ וְנִלְחַ֖ם עִם־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֥י הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And said David to Saul, Let not fall [the] heart of a man on account of him; your servant will go and fight with this Philistine.
pieces: David said to Saul, "No one should lose heart because of this man! Your servant will go and fight this Philistine."

L.32: And David said to Saul, "Let no man's heart fall because of him; your servant will go and fight with this Philistine."

R.32: David said to Saul, "Nobody should be afraid because of this Philistine. I will go and fight him myself!"

decisions.choice: let no man's heart fall: let no one lose courage
decisions.reason: For the heart to fall is to lose courage. David speaks to the fear of verses 11 and 24.

decisions.choice: no man's heart
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation reads "let not my lord's heart fall", so that David speaks to Saul's own fear. The received Hebrew text says "no man's heart". This is given from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against a critical edition.

decisions.choice: your servant: a polite way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: Speaking to the king, David calls himself "your servant" (also verses 34 and 36). It is the courtesy of a subject, not a statement that he is a slave.

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: Readable uses "I" for the polite "your servant" here and in verses 34 and 36.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֜וּל אֶל־דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תוּכַל֙ לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֣י הַזֶּ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם עִמּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־נַ֣עַר אַ֔תָּה וְה֛וּא אִ֥ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֖ה מִנְּעֻרָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: And said Saul to David, Not you will be able to go to this Philistine to fight with him, for a youth [are] you, and he [is] a man of war from his youth.
pieces: Saul answered David, "You cannot go out against this Philistine and fight him. You are a mere youth, and he has been trained for war since his own youth."

L.33: And Saul said to David, "You are not able to go against this Philistine to fight with him, for you [are] a youth, and he [is] a man of war from his youth."

R.33: Saul said, "You cannot fight this Philistine. You are just a young man, and he has been a soldier all his life."

decisions.choice: a youth: a young man
decisions.reason: The word names a boy or young man, often one not yet a seasoned soldier. Saul uses it twice, of David now and of Goliath in his early years: the giant has been at war longer than David has been alive. The same word is used of David in verses 42, 55 and 58.

decisions.choice: a man of war: a trained warrior
decisions.reason: The phrase means a professional soldier (Joshua 17:1). Ironically, 16:18 had already called David "a man of war".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־שָׁא֔וּל רֹעֶ֨ה הָיָ֧ה עַבְדְּךָ֛ לְאָבִ֖יו בַּצֹּ֑אן וּבָ֤א הָֽאֲרִי֙ וְאֶת־הַדּ֔וֹב וְנָשָׂ֥א שֶׂ֖ה מֵהָעֵֽדֶר׃
records.gloss: And said David to Saul, A shepherd has been your servant for his father among the flock, and came the lion and the bear and carried off a sheep from the flock,
pieces: But David said to Saul, "Your servant has been a shepherd for his father's flock, and any time a lion or a bear would come and carry off a sheep from the flock,

L.34: And David said to Saul, "Your servant has been a shepherd for his father among the flock, and [when] the lion or the bear would come and carry off a sheep from the flock,

R.34: But David said to Saul, "I have been taking care of my father's sheep. Sometimes a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep from the flock.

decisions.choice: came ... carried off: what happened from time to time
decisions.reason: The verbs here and in verse 35 describe what used to happen: whenever a wild animal took a sheep, David went after it. They could also tell of one occasion when both a lion and a bear came.

decisions.choice: your servant: as in verse 32
decisions.reason: David continues to speak of himself politely as "your servant".

decisions.choice: the lion and the bear: wild animals of the land
decisions.reason: Lions and bears lived in the hills and thickets of Israel at this time (Judges 14:5; 2 Kings 2:24). A shepherd was expected to defend the flock (Genesis 31:39; Amos 3:12).

decisions.choice: I
decisions.reason: As in verse 32.

records.source: וְיָצָ֧אתִי אַחֲרָ֛יו וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וְהִצַּ֣לְתִּי מִפִּ֑יו וַיָּ֣קָם עָלַ֔י וְהֶחֱזַ֨קְתִּי֙ בִּזְקָנ֔וֹ וְהִכִּתִ֖יו וַהֲמִיתִּֽיו׃
records.gloss: and I went out after it and struck it and rescued [it] from its mouth; and it rose up against me, and I took hold of its beard and struck it and killed it.
pieces: I went after it, struck it, and rescued the sheep from its mouth. If it turned on me, I grabbed it by its jaw, struck it and killed it.

L.35: and I would go out after it and strike it and rescue [it] from its mouth; and [if] it rose up against me, I would seize [it] by its beard and strike it and kill it.

R.35: I went after it, hit it, and saved the sheep from its mouth. If the animal turned and attacked me, I grabbed it by its jaw and hit it until it died.

decisions.choice: its beard: the hair of its chin, its jaw
decisions.reason: The word means beard or chin. Of a lion or bear it means the jaw or the hair under it, where David seized the animal.

decisions.choice: it rose up against me: if it turned to attack
decisions.reason: The clause states what happened if the animal attacked David instead of running.

decisions.choice: jaw
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "jaw", since "beard" sounds odd for a wild animal.

records.source: גַּ֧ם אֶֽת־הָאֲרִ֛י גַּם־הַדּ֖וֹב הִכָּ֣ה עַבְדֶּ֑ךָ וְֽ֠הָיָה הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֨י הֶעָרֵ֤ל הַזֶּה֙ כְּאַחַ֣ד מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י חֵרֵ֔ף מַעַרְכֹ֖ת אֱלֹהִ֥ים חַיִּֽים׃ס
records.gloss: Both the lion and the bear your servant has struck down; and will be this uncircumcised Philistine like one of them, for he has defied [the] ranks of [the] living God.
pieces: Lions and bears alike your servant has killed, and this uncircumcised Philistine will end up like one of them, since he has defied the ranks of the living God."

L.36: Both the lion and the bear your servant has struck down; and this uncircumcised Philistine will be like one of them, for he has defied the ranks of the living God."

R.36: I have killed lions and bears, and this Philistine, who is outside God's covenant, will end up just like them. He has insulted the army of the living God!"

decisions.choice: for he has defied the ranks of the living God: David's reason for confidence
decisions.reason: David's courage does not rest on his skill but on the fact that Goliath has insulted the living God (verse 26). God's honor is at stake, so David expects God to act.

decisions.choice: the lion and the bear: such animals
decisions.reason: The article points to the kinds of animal David spoke of in verse 34, not to one lion and one bear only.

decisions.choice: I; who is outside God's covenant
decisions.reason: Readable uses "I" as in verse 32 and explains "uncircumcised" as in verse 26.

records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ דָּוִד֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּלַ֜נִי מִיַּ֤ד הָֽאֲרִי֙ וּמִיַּ֣ד הַדֹּ֔ב ה֣וּא יַצִּילֵ֔נִי מִיַּ֥ד הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י הַזֶּ֑הסוַיֹּ֨אמֶר שָׁא֤וּל אֶל־דָּוִד֙ לֵ֔ךְ וַֽיהוָ֖ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And said David, Yahweh who delivered me from [the] hand of the lion and from [the] hand of the bear, he will deliver me from [the] hand of this Philistine. And said Saul to David, Go, and Yahweh will be with you.
pieces: David went on, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} rescued me from the power of the lion and of the bear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue me from the power of this Philistine." Then Saul said to David, "Go. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."

L.37: And David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." And Saul said to David, "Go, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be with you."

R.37: David said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kept me safe from the lion and the bear, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will keep me safe from this Philistine too." Then Saul said to David, "Go, and may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} be with you."

decisions.choice: Yahweh delivered me ... he will deliver me
decisions.reason: David gives the credit for his past victories to Yahweh, and rests his hope for this fight on the same God. The fight will show that the battle belongs to Yahweh (verse 47).

decisions.choice: the hand: the power, the grip
decisions.reason: "Hand" often means power or control. Of the lion and the bear it is their grip, their claws.

decisions.choice: Yahweh will be with you: a wish
alternatives: a statement: Yahweh will be with you
decisions.reason: The form can be a statement or a wish; on Saul's lips it is a blessing. The narrator has already said that Yahweh was with David (16:18), and will say it again (18:12, 14).

decisions.choice: power
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "power" for "hand" to fit the animals as well as the Philistine; Readable says "kept me safe from".

records.heading: David goes out to meet the Philistine

records.source: וַיַּלְבֵּ֨שׁ שָׁא֤וּל אֶת־דָּוִד֙ מַדָּ֔יו וְנָתַ֛ן ק֥וֹבַע נְחֹ֖שֶׁת עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיַּלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֹת֖וֹ שִׁרְיֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And clothed Saul David [in] his garments, and put a helmet of bronze on his head, and clothed him [in] armor.
pieces: Saul dressed David in his own battle clothes. He put a bronze helmet on his head and fitted him with a coat of armor.

L.38: And Saul clothed David [in] his garments and put a helmet of bronze on his head and clothed him [in] armor.

R.38: Then Saul dressed David in his own soldier's clothing. He put a bronze helmet on David's head and put armor on him.

decisions.choice: his garments: Saul's own battle tunic
decisions.reason: The word names a garment, here the tunic worn under armor (18:4). "His" is Saul's: the king gives David what he himself should be wearing to face Goliath.

decisions.choice: armor: a coat of mail
decisions.reason: This is the same kind of scale armor that Goliath wore (verse 5).

decisions.choice: battle clothes; soldier's clothing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these were the clothes worn for battle.

records.source: וַיַּחְגֹּ֣ר דָּוִ֣ד אֶת־חַ֠רְבּוֹ מֵעַ֨ל לְמַדָּ֜יו וַיֹּ֣אֶל לָלֶכֶת֮ כִּ֣י לֹֽא־נִסָּה֒ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד אֶל־שָׁא֗וּל לֹ֥א אוּכַ֛ל לָלֶ֥כֶת בָּאֵ֖לֶּה כִּ֣י לֹ֣א נִסִּ֑יתִי וַיְסִרֵ֥ם דָּוִ֖ד מֵעָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And girded David his sword over his garments and undertook to walk, for not he had tested; and said David to Saul, Not I am able to walk in these, for not I have tested; and removed them David from upon him.
pieces: David buckled Saul's sword over the clothes and tried to move about, since he had never worn such gear. Then he said to Saul, "I cannot walk in all this; I have not tried it before." And David took it all off.

L.39: And David fastened his sword over his garments and tried to walk, for he had not tested [them]. And David said to Saul, "I cannot walk in these, for I have not tested [them]." And David took them off.

R.39: David put on Saul's sword over the soldier's clothing and tried to walk around, but he had never practiced in armor. He said to Saul, "I cannot move in these things. I have never used them." So David took them off.

decisions.choice: tested: tried out, got used to
decisions.reason: The verb means to test or try something by practice. David had never trained in armor, so it would hinder rather than help him.

decisions.choice: his sword: Saul's sword
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to Saul, who is dressing David in his own gear (verse 38). David will later use Goliath's sword (verse 51).

decisions.choice: Saul's sword
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the owner of the sword.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח מַקְל֜וֹ בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּבְחַר־ל֣וֹ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה חַלֻּקֵֽי־אֲבָנִ֣ים׀מִן־הַנַּ֡חַל וַיָּ֣שֶׂם אֹ֠תָם בִּכְלִ֨י הָרֹעִ֧ים אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וּבַיַּלְק֖וּט וְקַלְּע֣וֹ בְיָד֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֖שׁ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth [ones of] stones from the wadi, and put them in the bag of the shepherds which [was] to him, and in the pouch, and his sling [was] in his hand; and he drew near to the Philistine.
pieces: He took his staff in his hand, picked out five smooth stones from the streambed, and put them in his shepherd's bag, in its pouch. Then, with his sling in his hand, he went toward the Philistine.

L.40: And he took his staff in his hand and chose for himself five smooth stones from the wadi, and put them in the shepherd's bag that [was] his, in the pouch; and his sling [was] in his hand, and he drew near to the Philistine.

R.40: David took his shepherd's stick in his hand. He chose five smooth stones from the dry streambed and put them in the pouch of his shepherd's bag. Then, holding his sling, he went out to meet the Philistine.

decisions.choice: the wadi: a streambed
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley stream that runs with water in the rainy season and is dry the rest of the year. Its stones are worn smooth by the water, so they fly true from a sling.

decisions.choice: the pouch: the shepherd's bag
decisions.reason: This word is found only here. It seems to explain the "shepherd's bag" just named: a leather pouch carried over the shoulder for food and small things.

decisions.choice: sling: a weapon, not a toy
decisions.reason: A sling was a cord with a pocket in the middle, whirled to hurl a stone with great force. Trained slingers were part of ancient armies and could hit a target with deadly aim (Judges 20:16).

decisions.choice: shepherd's stick
decisions.reason: Readable explains what kind of staff David carried.

records.source: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְקָרֵ֖ב אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד וְהָאִ֛ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֥א הַצִּנָּ֖ה לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And came the Philistine, going and drawing near to David, and the man bearing the shield before him.
pieces: The Philistine came on, drawing closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer in front of him.

L.41: And the Philistine came, coming nearer and nearer to David, and the man carrying the shield [was] before him.

R.41: The Philistine kept coming closer to David, and the man carrying his shield walked in front of him.

decisions.choice: going and drawing near: coming steadily closer
decisions.reason: The two verbs together describe a steady advance.

decisions.choice: this verse is part of the received Hebrew text
decisions.reason: This verse is one of those missing from the shorter text of the ancient Greek translation; see verse 12.

records.source: וַיַּבֵּ֧ט הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י וַיִּרְאֶ֥ה אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד וַיִּבְזֵ֑הוּ כִּֽי־הָיָ֣ה נַ֔עַר וְאַדְמֹנִ֖י עִם־יְפֵ֥ה מַרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And looked the Philistine and saw David and despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy with handsome of appearance.
pieces: When the Philistine looked David over, he scorned him, because he was only a youth, ruddy and handsome.

L.42: And the Philistine looked and saw David, and he despised him, for he was a youth, and ruddy, with a handsome appearance.

R.42: Goliath looked David over and thought nothing of him. He was just a young man, with a healthy glow and good looks.

decisions.choice: ruddy and handsome: as in 16:12
decisions.reason: The words repeat the description of David when Samuel anointed him (16:12). Goliath judges by appearance and sees only a boy, just as Samuel was warned not to judge by outward looks (16:7).

decisions.choice: ruddy: of reddish color
decisions.reason: The word means reddish. It may describe a healthy, fresh complexion or reddish hair (Genesis 25:25).

decisions.choice: despised him: looked on him with contempt
decisions.reason: To despise is to count someone as worthless. Goliath thinks the fight is beneath him.

decisions.choice: Goliath; thought nothing of him; a healthy glow
decisions.reason: Readable names the Philistine and uses everyday words for his scorn and for "ruddy".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ אֶל־דָּוִ֔ד הֲכֶ֣לֶב אָנֹ֔כִי כִּֽי־אַתָּ֥ה בָֽא־אֵלַ֖י בַּמַּקְל֑וֹת וַיְקַלֵּ֧ל הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־דָּוִ֖ד בֵּאלֹהָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said the Philistine to David, [Am] I a dog, that you come to me with sticks? And cursed the Philistine David by his gods.
pieces: "Am I some dog, that you come after me with sticks?" the Philistine said to David, and he called down curses on David by his gods.

L.43: And the Philistine said to David, "Am I a dog, that you come to me with sticks?" And the Philistine cursed David by his gods.

R.43: He said to David, "Do you think I am a dog? Is that why you are coming at me with sticks?" Then he called on his gods to curse David.

decisions.choice: a dog: a despised animal
decisions.reason: Dogs in Israel were scavengers, not pets. To call a person a dog was an insult (24:15; 2 Samuel 9:8). Goliath takes David's staff as an insult to a warrior.

decisions.choice: sticks: in scorn
decisions.reason: David carries one staff (verse 40), but Goliath speaks of "sticks". The plural may be mockery or exaggeration.

decisions.choice: his gods: the Philistine gods
decisions.reason: The word for God has a plural form; here, used by a Philistine, it means the gods of his people, such as Dagon (5:2). It could also be read "his god".

decisions.choice: Do you think I am a dog? Is that why ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the one question into two short ones.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־דָּוִ֑ד לְכָ֣ה אֵלַ֔י וְאֶתְּנָה֙ אֶת־בְּשָׂ֣רְךָ֔ לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְבֶהֱמַ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And said the Philistine to David, Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the field.
pieces: The Philistine said to David, "Come over here to me, and I will feed your body to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field!"

L.44: And the Philistine said to David, "Come to me, and I will give your flesh to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the field."

R.44: The Philistine said to David, "Come here, and I will feed your body to the birds and the wild animals!"

decisions.choice: your flesh to the birds and beasts: death without burial
decisions.reason: To have one's body left unburied for birds and wild animals was the worst disgrace (Deuteronomy 28:26; 2 Samuel 21:10). David turns this threat back on the Philistine army (verse 46).

decisions.choice: feed your body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "body" for "flesh" and give the sense of "give to".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אַתָּה֙ בָּ֣א אֵלַ֔י בְּחֶ֖רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֣ית וּבְכִיד֑וֹן וְאָנֹכִ֣י בָֽא־אֵלֶ֗יךָ בְּשֵׁם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֛י מַעַרְכ֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר חֵרַֽפְתָּ׃
records.gloss: And said David to the Philistine, You come to me with sword and with spear and with javelin, and I come to you in [the] name of Yahweh of hosts, [the] God of [the] ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.
pieces: David said to the Philistine, "You have come out against me with a sword, a spear and a javelin. I have come out against you in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, the God of Israel's ranks, the one you have defied.

L.45: And David said to the Philistine, "You come to me with sword and with spear and with javelin, but I come to you in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel, whom you have defied.

R.45: David answered the Philistine, "You are coming to fight me with a sword, a spear and a javelin. But I am coming to fight you in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: in the name of Yahweh of hosts: with his authority and trusting his power
decisions.reason: To come in someone's name is to act as his representative and to rely on him (Psalm 20:8). David's weapon is not his sling but Yahweh.

decisions.choice: of hosts: of armies
decisions.reason: The word means armies or hosts. The title presents Yahweh as commander of all forces, those of heaven and of Israel (1:3; 4:4). Here it is set beside "the God of the ranks of Israel": the army Goliath has taunted is God's own.

decisions.choice: sword, spear and javelin
decisions.reason: David names the weapons described in verses 5-7. Verse 47 answers them: Yahweh does not save by sword and spear.

decisions.choice: of hosts (Literal); of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "hosts"; Balanced and Readable say "Armies", which makes the link with "the ranks of Israel" clear.

records.source: הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֡ה יְסַגֶּרְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה בְּיָדִ֜י וְהִכִּיתִ֗ךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֤י אֶת־רֹֽאשְׁךָ֙ מֵעָלֶ֔יךָ וְנָ֨תַתִּ֜י פֶּ֣גֶר מַחֲנֵ֤ה פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה לְע֥וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וּלְחַיַּ֣ת הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: This day will deliver you up Yahweh into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from upon you, and I will give [the] corpse[s] of [the] army of [the] Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the animals of the earth; and will know all the earth that there is a God for Israel,
pieces: Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will hand you over to me. I will strike you down and cut off your head, and this very day I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a God,

L.46: This day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will deliver you into my hand, and I will strike you down and remove your head from you, and I will give the corpses of the army of the Philistines this day to the birds of the heavens and to the beasts of the earth, so that all the earth may know that there is a God in Israel,

R.46: Today {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will put you in my power. I will kill you and cut off your head. And today I will give the bodies of the Philistine soldiers to the birds and the wild animals. Then everyone in the world will know that there is a God who fights for Israel.

decisions.choice: the corpses to the birds and beasts: Goliath's threat turned back
decisions.reason: David answers Goliath's threat of verse 44 with the same words, now aimed at the whole Philistine army.

decisions.choice: deliver you up into my hand: hand you over to my power
decisions.reason: The verb means to shut up or hand over. Yahweh will give Goliath into David's power.

decisions.choice: all the earth will know that there is a God for Israel
alternatives: there is a God in Israel
decisions.reason: The victory will show the nations that Israel's God is real and acts for his people, as the plagues and the crossing of the Jordan were to do (Exodus 9:14, 16; Joshua 4:24). The phrase can be read "there is a God in Israel" or "Israel has a God"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a God who fights for Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes explicit that the God of Israel shows himself by acting for Israel, as verse 47 says.

records.source: וְיֵֽדְעוּ֙ כָּל־הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה כִּֽי־לֹ֛א בְּחֶ֥רֶב וּבַחֲנִ֖ית יְהוֹשִׁ֣יעַ יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ הַמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנָתַ֥ן אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּיָדֵֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: and will know all this assembly that not by sword and by spear saves Yahweh; for to Yahweh [is] the battle, and he will give you into our hand.
pieces: and everyone gathered here will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not save by sword or spear. The battle belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will hand you over to us."

L.47: and all this assembly may know that not with sword and with spear does {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} save; for the battle [belongs] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you into our hand."

R.47: And everyone here will know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} does not need a sword or a spear to save {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. The battle belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will help us defeat all of you."

decisions.choice: this assembly: all who are gathered here
decisions.reason: The word usually means Israel gathered as a people. Here it is the army of Israel assembled in the valley, and perhaps the Philistines watching too.

decisions.choice: Yahweh does not save by sword and spear
decisions.reason: Victory comes from Yahweh, not from weapons (Psalm 33:16-17; Hosea 1:7). Jonathan said the same in 14:6.

decisions.choice: the battle belongs to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The war is Yahweh's own; he fights for Israel (Exodus 14:14; 2 Chronicles 20:15).

decisions.choice: you: all of you
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural: Yahweh will give the whole Philistine army into Israel's power.

decisions.choice: to save his people; help us defeat all of you
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Yahweh saves and what giving "into our hand" means.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ כִּֽי־קָ֣ם הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיִּקְרַ֖ב לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֑ד וַיְמַהֵ֣ר דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּ֥רָץ הַמַּעֲרָכָ֖ה לִקְרַ֥את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And it was, when arose the Philistine and came and drew near to meet David, and hurried David and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.
pieces: As the Philistine moved forward and came closer to meet David, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him.

L.48: And it happened, when the Philistine arose and came and drew near to meet David, that David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet the Philistine.

R.48: The Philistine moved in to attack David, and David ran fast toward the enemy line to meet him.

decisions.choice: toward the battle line: toward the enemy
decisions.reason: David runs toward the Philistine ranks, meeting the giant head on, while Israel's soldiers had run away from him (verse 24).

decisions.choice: David hurried and ran
decisions.reason: This second half of the verse is missing from the shorter text of the ancient Greek translation; see verse 12.

decisions.choice: to attack him
decisions.reason: Readable says why the Philistine came forward.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד אֶת־יָד֜וֹ אֶל־הַכֶּ֗לִי וַיִּקַּ֨ח מִשָּׁ֥ם אֶ֨בֶן֙ וַיְקַלַּ֔ע וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י אֶל־מִצְח֑וֹ וַתִּטְבַּ֤ע הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ בְּמִצְח֔וֹ וַיִּפֹּ֥ל עַל־פָּנָ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃
records.gloss: And stretched out David his hand into the bag and took from there a stone and slung [it] and struck the Philistine on his forehead; and sank the stone into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.
pieces: David reached into his bag, took out a stone, slung it, and hit the Philistine in the forehead. The stone buried itself in his forehead, and he crashed face down to the ground.

L.49: And David put his hand into the bag and took a stone from there and slung [it] and struck the Philistine on his forehead; and the stone sank into his forehead, and he fell on his face to the ground.

R.49: David reached into his bag, took out a stone, and threw it with his sling. It hit the Philistine on the forehead and went deep into his head. Goliath fell on his face to the ground.

decisions.choice: his forehead: the place his armor left open
decisions.reason: Goliath's armor is described in detail (verses 5-7), but his face was uncovered, and the stone struck there.

decisions.choice: he fell on his face to the ground
decisions.reason: The words recall Dagon, the Philistine god, fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of Yahweh (5:3-4).

decisions.choice: buried itself; went deep into his head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the force of the blow in natural words.

records.source: וַיֶּחֱזַ֨ק דָּוִ֤ד מִן־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּי֙ בַּקֶּ֣לַע וּבָאֶ֔בֶן וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י וַיְמִיתֵ֑הוּ וְחֶ֖רֶב אֵ֥ין בְּיַד־דָּוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And was strong David over the Philistine with the sling and with the stone, and struck down the Philistine and killed him; and a sword there was not in [the] hand of David.
pieces: So David overcame the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck the Philistine down and killed him, though David had no sword in his hand.

L.50: So David prevailed over the Philistine with the sling and with the stone, and he struck down the Philistine and killed him; and there was no sword in David's hand.

R.50: That is how David defeated the Philistine with only a sling and a stone. He struck him down and killed him without even having a sword.

decisions.choice: struck down and killed him: a summary of the victory
decisions.reason: This verse sums up the outcome; verse 51 then tells in detail how David finished Goliath off with the giant's own sword. The stone brought him down, and the sword made his death certain.

decisions.choice: no sword in David's hand
decisions.reason: The point is the one David made in verse 47: Yahweh does not save by sword and spear. Saul's army had few swords (13:22), and David refused Saul's (verse 39).

decisions.choice: this verse is part of the received Hebrew text
decisions.reason: This verse is one of those missing from the shorter text of the ancient Greek translation; see verse 12.

decisions.choice: only; without even
decisions.reason: Readable brings out the contrast between David's weapons and Goliath's.

records.source: וַיָּ֣רָץ דָּ֠וִד וַיַּעֲמֹ֨ד אֶל־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜י וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־חַ֠רְבּוֹ וַֽיִּשְׁלְפָ֤הּ מִתַּעְרָהּ֙ וַיְמֹ֣תְתֵ֔הוּ וַיִּכְרָת־בָּ֖הּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּרְא֧וּ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֛ים כִּֽי־מֵ֥ת גִּבּוֹרָ֖ם וַיָּנֻֽסוּ׃
records.gloss: And ran David and stood over the Philistine, and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and cut off with it his head; and saw the Philistines that had died their mighty one, and they fled.
pieces: David ran and stood over the Philistine. He took hold of the Philistine's sword, drew it from its sheath, and finished him off; and with it he cut off his head. Seeing that their champion was dead, the Philistines ran.

L.51: And David ran and stood over the Philistine and took his sword and drew it out of its sheath and killed him, and he cut off his head with it. And the Philistines saw that their mighty man was dead, and they fled.

R.51: David ran and stood over him. He pulled Goliath's own sword out of its sheath, killed him with it, and cut off his head. When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they ran away.

decisions.choice: his sword: Goliath's sword
decisions.reason: David had no sword (verse 50), so he used the giant's own. It was later kept at the sanctuary at Nob, and David took it again (21:10).

decisions.choice: killed him: finished him off
decisions.reason: The verb form here means to put to death, to make sure of death. Goliath was down but perhaps still alive.

decisions.choice: their mighty man: their champion
decisions.reason: The word means a mighty warrior, a hero. It names the one in whom the Philistines trusted.

decisions.choice: they fled
decisions.reason: The Philistines do not keep the terms of verse 9 and become Israel's slaves; they run.

decisions.choice: the Philistine's sword; Goliath's own sword
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose sword David used.

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֣מוּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל וִיהוּדָ֜ה וַיָּרִ֗עוּ וַֽיִּרְדְּפוּ֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים עַד־בּוֹאֲךָ֣ גַ֔יְא וְעַ֖ד שַׁעֲרֵ֣י עֶקְר֑וֹן וַֽיִּפְּל֞וּ חַֽלְלֵ֤י פְלִשְׁתִּים֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ שַׁעֲרַ֔יִם וְעַד־גַּ֖ת וְעַד־עֶקְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And arose [the] men of Israel and Judah and shouted [the] war cry and pursued the Philistines until your coming [to] a valley, and to [the] gates of Ekron; and fell [the] slain of [the] Philistines on [the] way of Shaaraim, and to Gath and to Ekron.
pieces: Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up with a shout and chased the Philistines as far as the valley and the gates of Ekron. Philistine dead lay along the Shaaraim road all the way to Gath and Ekron.

L.52: And the men of Israel and Judah arose and shouted the war cry and pursued the Philistines until [one] comes to a valley and to the gates of Ekron; and the slain of the Philistines fell on the road of Shaaraim, as far as Gath and Ekron.

R.52: Then the soldiers of Israel and Judah jumped up and shouted their battle cry. They chased the Philistines all the way to the valley and to the gates of the city of Ekron. Dead Philistines lay along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.

decisions.choice: a valley
decisions.reason: The received Hebrew text reads "a valley". The ancient Greek translation reads "Gath", which would pair with Ekron as at the end of the verse. This note is given from general knowledge; reviewers must check it against a critical edition.

decisions.choice: Shaaraim: a town of Judah's lowland
decisions.reason: Shaaraim is listed with Socoh and Azekah (Joshua 15:35-36). The road from there led west toward the Philistine cities.

decisions.choice: Gath and Ekron: Philistine cities
decisions.reason: These were two of the five Philistine cities (6:17), on the coastal plain west of the Valley of Elah. Israel chased the Philistines back to their own gates.

decisions.choice: Israel and Judah: the whole people
decisions.reason: Judah is named alongside Israel, as in 11:8 and 15:4, perhaps because the battle was fought in Judah's land (verse 1).
