decisions.choice: as far as; all the way to
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the Hebrew idiom "until your coming to".

records.source: וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מִדְּלֹ֖ק אַחֲרֵ֣י פְלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיָּשֹׁ֖סּוּ אֶת־מַחֲנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And returned [the] sons of Israel from hotly pursuing after [the] Philistines and plundered their camps.
pieces: When the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came back from chasing the Philistines, they plundered their camp.

L.53: And the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel returned from hotly pursuing the Philistines and plundered their camps.

R.53: After the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} came back from chasing the Philistines, they took everything of value from the Philistine camp.

decisions.choice: hotly pursuing: chasing fiercely
decisions.reason: The verb means to burn or to pursue hotly, a hard and eager chase.

decisions.choice: plundered: took the goods left behind
decisions.reason: The fleeing army left its camp, and Israel took the spoil.

decisions.choice: took everything of value
decisions.reason: Readable explains "plundered".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֤ח דָּוִד֙ אֶת־רֹ֣אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְאֶת־כֵּלָ֖יו שָׂ֥ם בְּאָהֳלֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And took David the head of the Philistine and brought it [to] Jerusalem, and his weapons he put in his tent.
pieces: David took the Philistine's head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put the Philistine's weapons in his own tent.

L.54: And David took the head of the Philistine and brought it [to] Jerusalem, and he put his weapons in his tent.

R.54: David took Goliath's head and brought it to Jerusalem. He kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem: a city not yet in Israel's hands
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was held by the Jebusites until David captured it as king (2 Samuel 5:6-9). The verse may look ahead to that time, telling where the trophy was finally kept, or Israelites may already have lived there beside the Jebusites (Judges 1:8, 21). The text does not explain.

decisions.choice: his tent: David's own tent
decisions.reason: The word can mean a soldier's tent or a dwelling. David kept the weapons as his spoil. Goliath's sword later appears at the sanctuary at Nob (21:10), so David may have given it there afterward.

decisions.choice: the Philistine's weapons; Goliath's weapons
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whose weapons these were.

records.source: וְכִרְא֨וֹת שָׁא֜וּל אֶת־דָּוִ֗ד יֹצֵא֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י אָמַ֗ר אֶל־אַבְנֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א בֶּן־מִי־זֶ֥ה הַנַּ֖עַר אַבְנֵ֑ר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אַבְנֵ֔ר חֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֥ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אִם־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And when saw Saul David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, commander of the army, Whose son [is] this youth, Abner? And said Abner, [By the] life of your soul, O king, if I know.
pieces: When Saul had watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he had asked Abner, the commander of the army, "Whose son is this young man, Abner?" Abner replied, "As surely as you live, O king, I do not know."

L.55: And when Saul saw David going out to meet the Philistine, he said to Abner, the commander of the army, "Whose son [is] this youth, Abner?" And Abner said, "[As] your soul lives, O king, I do not know."

R.55: Earlier, when Saul saw David going out to fight the Philistine, he had asked Abner, the army commander, "Abner, whose son is this young man?" Abner answered, "Your Majesty, I promise you that I do not know."

decisions.choice: when Saul saw David going out: a look back
decisions.reason: Verses 55-56 go back to the moment before the fight, when David went out to meet Goliath. Verses 57-58 return to the time after it.

decisions.choice: whose son is this youth?: Saul asks about David's family
decisions.reason: Saul had promised the winner his daughter and freedom for his father's house (verse 25), so he needed to know who the young man's father was. Yet in 16:18-23 Saul had already sent to Jesse and taken David into his service. The story does not explain this; the account may come from a separate telling (see verse 12), or Saul may not have connected the shepherd boy with his musician.

decisions.choice: as your soul lives ... I do not know: an oath
decisions.reason: Abner swears by the king's life. In such oaths "if I know" means "I do not know": the curse that would follow if it were false is left unsaid.

decisions.choice: verses 55-58 are part of the received Hebrew text
decisions.reason: Verses 55-58, with the opening verses of chapter 18, are missing from the shorter text of the ancient Greek translation; see verse 12.

decisions.choice: had watched ... had asked; Earlier
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that these words look back to before the fight.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty
decisions.reason: Readable uses a modern form of address to a king.

records.heading: Saul asks whose son David is

records.source: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׁאַ֣ל אַתָּ֔ה בֶּן־מִי־זֶ֖ה הָעָֽלֶם׃ס
records.gloss: And said the king, Ask you whose son this young man [is].
pieces: The king said, "Find out whose son this young man is."

L.56: And the king said, "You ask whose son this young man [is]."

R.56: The king said, "Find out who this young man's father is."

decisions.choice: young man: a youth of marriageable age
decisions.reason: This is a different word from the "youth" of verse 55. It names a young man grown to manhood.

decisions.choice: ask you: you find out
decisions.reason: The added pronoun stresses that Abner himself is to find out.

records.source: וּכְשׁ֣וּב דָּוִ֗ד מֵֽהַכּוֹת֙ אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ לִפְנֵ֣י שָׁא֑וּל וְרֹ֥אשׁ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And when returned David from striking down the Philistine, took him Abner and brought him before Saul, and the head of the Philistine [was] in his hand.
pieces: As soon as David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him to Saul, with the Philistine's head still in his hand.

L.57: And when David returned from striking down the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him before Saul, with the head of the Philistine in his hand.

R.57: As soon as David came back from killing Goliath, Abner brought him to Saul. David was still holding Goliath's head.

decisions.choice: in his hand: David's hand
decisions.reason: David comes before the king still holding the giant's head, the proof of his victory.

decisions.choice: Goliath
decisions.reason: Readable uses the name instead of "the Philistine".

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ שָׁא֔וּל בֶּן־מִ֥י אַתָּ֖ה הַנָּ֑עַר וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֔ד בֶּֽן־עַבְדְּךָ֥ יִשַׁ֖י בֵּ֥ית הַלַּחְמִֽי׃
records.gloss: And said to him Saul, Whose son [are] you, young man? And said David, [The] son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite.
pieces: Saul asked him, "Whose son are you, young man?" "The son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem," David answered.

L.58: And Saul said to him, "Whose son [are] you, young man?" And David said, "[The] son of your servant Jesse the Bethlehemite."

R.58: Saul asked him, "Young man, who is your father?" David answered, "I am the son of your servant Jesse, from Bethlehem."

decisions.choice: your servant Jesse: a courteous form
decisions.reason: David speaks of his father as the king's servant, the respectful way for a subject to name someone to the king (verse 32).

decisions.choice: Jesse the Bethlehemite
decisions.reason: The chapter ends where David's story began, with Jesse of Bethlehem (16:1, 18). Saul now knows the family of the man who will one day take his place.

decisions.choice: who is your father?
decisions.reason: Readable asks the question in everyday words.
